questions.candidate_answer: I would handle API concurrency with asynchronous I/O for network calls and a bounded worker pool for CPU intensive tasks. questions.question_text: When scaling applications with PostgreSQL, how do you design tables and indexes for high-throughput reads and writes? How would you identify and fix a slow-running query in production?

questions.candidate_answer: I would design database indexes around frequent filters and joins, inspect the query plan and measure latency using representative data. To handle consistency I would use a transaction for related updates, validate inputs and test rollback paths. Indexes speed reads but consume storage and make writes more expensive, so I would retain only indexes justified by measurements.

questions.question_text: When scaling applications with PostgreSQL, how do you design tables and indexes for high-throughput reads and writes? How would you identify and fix a slow-running query in production?
questions.question_text_en: When scaling applications with PostgreSQL, how do you design tables and indexes for high-throughput reads and writes? How would you identify and fix a slow-running query in production?

questions.candidate_answer: I would design database indexes around frequent filters and joins, inspect the query plan and measure latency using representative data. To handle consistency I would use a transaction for related updates, validate inputs and test rollback paths. Indexes speed reads but consume storage and make writes more expensive, so I would retain only indexes justified by measurements.
